official.deadline_note: The call states applications received after 15 December 2025 will NOT be considered. No 2027 call dates have been published, though the cycle historically runs 15 November to 15 December.
official.application_cycle: 2026-2027 academic year; the call was launched on 15 November 2025 and closed on 15 December 2025
official.status_note: The official announcement and the PAU submission platform both state that the call closed on 15 December 2025 and that late applications will not be considered. The 2026-2027 cycle is therefore closed.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The announcement states only that 'The African Union Commission will offer full scholarships to successful candidates' and does not itemise what the full scholarship covers.
benefits: Full scholarships awarded by the African Union Commission (the announcement states the Commission will offer full scholarships to successful candidates)
Joint degree awards from the Pan African University and its host universities
Study at one of four PAU institutes: PAUSTI in Kenya, PAUGHSS in Cameroun, PAUWES in Algeria and PAULESI in Nigeria
eligibility: Applicants from African countries and the Diaspora
Master's: not older than 25 years for male and 28 years for female applicants
Master's: holder of an undergraduate degree from a recognised university, with at least a second-class upper division or its equivalent, in a relevant field
PhD: maximum 28 years old for male and 30 years old for female applicants
PhD: a master's degree in a relevant field from PAU or any internationally recognised university

Master's candidates for Conference Interpreting and Translation must have excellent knowledge of at least two of the African Union's official languages (Arabic, English, French, Portuguese, Kiswahili and Spanish)
Meet immigration and visa requirements for the host institute
requirements: Academic competence must be evidenced in academic transcripts at the bachelor's level
Candidates may be required to undergo a written or oral examination after pre-selection
Names and contact details of three reference university lecturers, with email address and WhatsApp number, are mandatory
Scholarship awardees should be committed to working in Africa after graduation
documents: Certified true copies of relevant certificates and transcripts, from university and high school
Passport or National Identity card, personal details page
Clear coloured passport size photograph, 2cm x 2cm
Master's: one recommendation letter from a former university lecturer
PhD: recommendation letters from two professors
PhD: a 3 to 4 page research concept note covering tentative title, research questions, objectives and significance of the research
selection_criteria: Candidates may be required to undergo a written or oral examination after pre-selection
Academic competence must be evidenced in the bachelor's-level transcripts
The announcement particularly encourages applicants who desire transformative leadership roles as academics, professionals, industrialists, innovators and entrepreneurs
coverage: The announcement states the African Union Commission will offer full scholarships to successful candidates, but does not itemise the components
application_method: Register on the PAU submission platform with a valid username and email
Check your inbox, including spam, and click the confirmation link to complete registration
Set a valid password and log in with your credentials
Open the Application page, provide all your data, click Save, and then click FINISH
If you do not finish, log in again later with the same email and password to continue
official.application_route: Register on the PAU submission portal, confirm the registration email, then complete and FINISH the online application; no paper application is accepted.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to applicants from African countries and the African Diaspora; no specific residency or nationality list of eligible countries is published.
official.international_eligibility: Open to applicants from African countries and the Diaspora, studying at PAU institutes hosted in Kenya, Cameroun, Algeria and Nigeria.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Master's and PhD programmes at the four PAU institutes (PAUSTI Basic Sciences, Technology and Innovation; PAUGHSS Governance, Humanities and Social Sciences; PAUWES Water and Energy Sciences including Climate Change; PAULESI Life and Earth Sciences including Health and Agriculture).
official.research_requirement: PhD applicants must submit a 3 to 4 page research concept note covering a tentative title, research questions, objectives and the significance of the research.
official.duration: Master's and PhD programmes at the Pan African University institutes; the announcement does not state programme length
official.description: The Pan African University is an initiative of the Heads of State and Government of the African Union, a premier continental university network whose mission is to provide quality postgraduate education geared towards a prosperous, integrated and peaceful Africa. From 2014 to date PAU has issued 2549 certificates to 856 females and 1693 males from 50 member states, and the African Union Commission offers full scholarships to successful candidates.

not_confirmed: funding_amount, funding_currency and funding_period - the announcement publishes no award value for the full scholarship
tuition_coverage, living_cost_coverage and travel_coverage - the announcement states only that full scholarships will be offered and does not itemise the components
english_requirement - no English test or score requirement is published; the only language rule is the two official languages requirement for the Master in Conference Interpreting and Translation
the 2027 cycle dates - only the 2026-2027 call (15 November to 15 December 2025) is published
programme length, and whether the scholarship covers the full master's or PhD duration
verification.notes: The full scholarship statement, all master's and PhD admission requirements, the document list, the deadline and the 'will NOT be considered' rule, the certificate statistics, and the step-by-step portal registration and submission procedure were read directly from the African Union announcement page and the official PAU submission platform.

applicant_utility.summary: This is one tight annual window, historically 15 November to 15 December, and the announcement is explicit that late applications will not be considered, so the practical deadline is the day the window closes rather than whenever you finish gathering documents. Your three reference lecturers must be listed with both an email address and a WhatsApp number, which is an unusual data requirement that routinely delays applications. The age limits are strict and gendered, with PhD applicants capped at 28 for men and 30 for women, so eligibility should be checked against the exact cut-off before investing in the full document set.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Young African graduates and postgraduates within the published age limits who want master's or PhD study at one of the four Pan African University institutes.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your age against the exact caps: 25 male / 28 female for master's, and 28 male / 30 female for PhD
Line up three reference lecturers early and collect both an email address and a WhatsApp number for each, since all three are mandatory
Have certificates and transcripts certified as true copies, including high school records, not just university ones
Prepare a 2cm x 2cm clear coloured passport photograph to the exact stated dimensions
PhD applicants: draft the 3 to 4 page concept note with tentative title, research questions, objectives and significance before opening the portal
Register on the portal early and immediately check spam for the confirmation email, since registration must be confirmed before you can log in
common_rejection_risks: Submitting after the 15 December close, which the announcement says will not be considered at any point
Exceeding the age limits, which are published per gender and are not waived
Failing to confirm the registration email, which blocks login and therefore submission
Omitting one of the three mandatory reference lecturers, or providing an email without a WhatsApp number
Leaving the application saved rather than clicking FINISH, which means it is never submitted
A bachelor's degree below a second-class upper division or equivalent, since academic competence must be evidenced at that level
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Not published: because the announcement does not itemise the scholarship, any shortfall in fees, living costs, travel or family support cannot be quantified from the official page.
document_audit: Both university and high school transcripts are required, so applicants who discarded school records early will need to obtain certified replacements
Certified true copies are required rather than plain photocopies or uncertified scans
The photograph must be 2cm x 2cm, coloured and clear, which is stricter than the usual generic passport photo
Reference lecturers must be listed with email and WhatsApp contact details, so referees need to be briefed on this before submission
PhD applicants need two professor recommendation letters plus the concept note, a heavier set than the master's single lecturer letter
alerts: The 2026-2027 call closed on 15 December 2025 and late applications are explicitly not considered, so the next realistic opportunity is the following November window
Registration must be confirmed by clicking the link sent to your email, so use an address you actively check and look in the spam folder
A written or oral examination may follow pre-selection, so a submitted application is not the final assessment stage
Awardees are expected to be committed to working in Africa after graduation, which is a stated condition rather than an informal expectation
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the PAU submission platform, confirm the email link, log in, complete the Application page, click Save and then FINISH, and await possible written or oral examination if pre-selected.
